newsitem.title: FRANCE: ETA's "intelligence chief" held in France.
newsitem.headline: ETA's "intelligence chief" held in France.

text.p: A Spaniard suspected of being the intelligence chief of the Basque guerrilla group ETA has been detained in southern France, police said on Thursday.
Igor Urrestarazu Garijo, a former municipal policeman in the Spanish Basque region, was detained in Albi on Tuesday after a car chase and later taken to anti-terrorist police headquarters in Paris.
He was carrying forged documents and was identified only after French police sent his fingerprints to Spain.

Spanish police said Urrestarazu began intelligence work for ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) in the Spanish Basque province of Guipuzcoa and took on a major role after he fled to France three years ago.

ETA has killed some 800 people in Spain in a three-decade-old campaign for a separate Basque state. Spanish authorities say its leaders are hiding in France and have asked Paris to redouble efforts to capture them.
ETA kidnapped and killed a Basque town councillor last month in an attempt to force the government to transfer all ETA inmates from prisons around the country to Basque prisons.
